capability.summary: Inspect metadata for an inactive legacy alias of npm_audit_json_exporter
capability.description: Inactive legacy manifest retained for compatibility metadata only. Its bundled script is behaviorally identical to npm_audit_json_exporter and must not be selected as a normal npm audit capability.
capability.problem_space: Compatibility inspection of an inactive, exactly duplicated npm-audit wrapper manifest; ordinary npm advisory audits route to active npm_audit_json_exporter instead.

env_requirements: a usable npm registry/network configuration and a supported lockfile in the resolved project directory
constraint.io_signature: Input: required file_path string naming an existing project directory or file; files resolve to their absolute parent directory. Executes `npm audit --json --prefix <dir>`. Output: JSON execution envelope with parsed npm report when available.
accepted_inputs: an existing file path whose parent directory is the intended npm project, typically package.json
constraint.output_shape: Retained legacy execution contract: npm exit 0 or 1 yields {status: "success", tool: "npm", target: string, exit_code: 0|1, result: JSON value|null, stdout: string|null, stderr: string|null}. The helper tries stdout then stderr; if stdout is non-JSON but stderr is one JSON document, result contains parsed stderr and stdout is still set to null. Other npm exits use status="tool_error" and propagate the exit code. Missing input, executable, or 180-second timeout yields {status: "error", tool: "npm", message: string}, exiting 2/3/4. This inactive alias is excluded from normal indexing.
limitations: inactive legacy duplicate retained only for metadata compatibility; use active npm_audit_json_exporter for ordinary audits
provides no distinct audit, package, license, policy, compliance, remediation, or source-analysis behavior
the retained helper parses stdout first and stderr second, and suppresses stdout whenever either stream parses as JSON; therefore non-JSON stdout can be lost when stderr contains JSON
legacy execution results depend on npm, registry, lockfile, network, authentication, and configuration and remain nondeterministic

output_contract.description: JSON execution envelope containing npm's parsed audit report when available, raw streams otherwise, and npm exit metadata.

intent_tags: identify legacy duplicate npm audit wrapper
inspect deprecated npm package auditor alias metadata
negative_intents: run a normal npm dependency audit
perform package license policy or compliance auditing
scan JavaScript source code for security bugs

output_contract.description: JSON execution envelope containing npm's parsed audit report when available, raw streams otherwise, and npm exit metadata.
